info.title: SEF Kopilot API
info.description:
Deterministic validation, plain-language explanations and reviewable repairs for Serbian (SEF)
and EU electronic invoices.

**This service is not a certified validator and is not affiliated with the Serbian Ministry of
Finance or the SEF platform.** By default it only ever talks to the public SEF *demo* environment.

get.description: Reports that the process is up, and whether it is a public demonstration. Never touches external dependencies.
Reports whether this instance can serve traffic. Each dependency is listed under `checks`; as soon as one of them fails the status is `degraded` and the response 503.

503.description: A dependency failed; the instance should not receive traffic.

post.summary: Create an account and its organization
post.description: Creates the account, an organization owned by it, and signs the person in.

429.description: Too many requests; try again after `Retry-After` seconds.

post.description: Checks the e-mail address and password and returns tokens for one organization. A member of several organizations names one in `organization_id`; without it the answer is 409 with the list to choose from.

post.summary: Join an organization with an invitation code
post.description: Redeems an invitation code: creates the account when the invited address has none, otherwise checks its password, then adds the membership and signs the person in to the organization. A code is good once.

429.description: Too many requests; try again after `Retry-After` seconds.

422.description: The new account's password is too short.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new pair
post.description: Spends the refresh token and returns a new access token and a new refresh token for the same session. A refresh token presented a second time ends the session.

429.description: Too many requests; try again after `Retry-After` seconds.

post.description: Ends the session of the refresh token; an unknown token changes nothing.

post.description: Validates the UBL 2.1 invoice or credit note in the request body against a profile and returns the validator's report. Nothing is stored: the document lives in memory for the length of the request (no-store mode). A document the validator cannot read is a violation in the report, not an error.

408.description: The invoice was not received in time.

413.description: The invoice has more bytes or elements than this server accepts.

422.description: The invoice could not be validated within the time limit, or the rule sets could not be applied to it.

429.description: Too many validations by the caller, or in their organization; try again after `Retry-After` seconds.

503.description: The validator is busy (retry after `Retry-After` seconds) or not available on this server.

requestBody.description: The invoice or credit note, UBL 2.1 XML.

post.description: Validates the invoice in the request body as `POST /invoices/validate` does, then explains each rule its report names: what the rule requires, why the invoice fails it and what to change, citing the passages of the official documents that apply on the invoice's issue date. Every citation is a passage of the corpus this server holds. Each rule is explained once, those that make the invoice invalid first, as many as the server allows in one request; a rule without an explanation says why. Nothing is stored. The language model is sent each rule's first violation, whose message may quote the invoice, and the passages; nothing else of the invoice.

post.description: Starts a job that validates again, with the rules this server has now, the stored invoices the caller may see, as `GET /invoices` lists them, and makes each new report the invoice's latest. `Location` names the job, which `GET /jobs/{job_id}` reads and `GET /jobs/{job_id}/events` follows. A member has one revalidation under way at a time. An invoice whose new report would take the organization past its quota keeps the report it has; the job counts it.

post.description: Explains each rule the stored invoice's latest report names, as `POST /invoices/explain` does for a document in the request body: what the rule requires, why the invoice fails it and what to change, citing the passages of the official documents that apply on the invoice's issue date. The invoice is not validated again: the report explained is the one `GET /invoices/{invoice_id}` reads, and comes with the answer. Nothing is stored. The language model is sent each rule's first violation, whose message may quote the invoice, and the passages; nothing else of the invoice. Counted as a request to the language model, not as a validation.

post.summary: Propose a repair of a stored invoice
post.description: Applies the patches to a copy of the stored invoice, in order, as `einvoice patch` does, validates what they leave under the invoice's profile, and keeps the repair: what became of each patch, the difference and the report. The invoice itself does not change until a person approves the repair. A patch that touches an amount, VAT, a tax or company identifier, a date or the document's number is not applied: it needs a person's decision. Counted as a validation. `Location` names the repair.

post.summary: Have the language model propose a repair of a stored invoice
post.description: Asks the language model for patches that repair the stored invoice's fatal violations, and keeps them as a repair the caller proposes: the invoice itself does not change until a person approves it. The model is sent the violations, whose messages may quote the invoice, and the invoice's fields around them, by canonical path; nothing else of it. Every answer is checked before anything is applied: each patch at a canonical path, writing no value the model was not given. The patches are applied to a copy and validated, as `POST /invoices/{invoice_id}/repairs` does; while fatal violations remain, the model is shown what became of each patch, for 2 rounds within the server's time limit. A patch that failed is not kept; one that touches an amount, VAT, a tax or company identifier, a date or the document's number is kept as needing a person's decision. Counted as a validation and as a request to the language model. `Location` names the repair.

post.description: A person approves the repair, in person: never with an API key. Its patches are applied again to the invoice, which must still be the document they were proposed for, and must leave the document they left then. The invoice becomes that document, with the validator's report on it, within the organization's storage quota; the other repairs that waited for the invoice are superseded. Counted as a validation.

get.description: Server-sent events: a `job` event with the job as `GET /jobs/{job_id}` reads it, at once and whenever the job changes. Each event's `id` is the job's `version`: a client that reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` is sent only what changed after it. The stream ends with the event of the finished job, or after five minutes, when the client reconnects. Comments keep a quiet stream open. A browser's `EventSource` cannot send an `Authorization` header: read the stream with `fetch`.
